subjective.question: H2O is given as text and you have to write 2 as subscript. How will you write it in HTML?

subjective.question: What are the types of lists in HTML?
subjective.answer: In HTML, there are three main types of lists: • Ordered List (<ol>) • Unordered List (<ul>) • Description List (<dl>)

subjective.question: Differentiate between Div and Span.
subjective.answer: <div> (Division): The <div> element is a block-level element, meaning it typically starts on a new line and takes up the full width available. It is used to group together HTML elements and create divisions or sections within a web page. <div> elements are often used to structure the layout of a webpage, such as defining sections, sidebars, headers, footers, etc. It is commonly styled with CSS to control its appearance, layout, and positioning. Examples: <div id="header">, <div class="sidebar">, <div class="container">. <span> (Inline Span): The <span> element is an inline-level element, meaning it does not start on a new line and only takes up as much width as its content requires. It is used to apply styles to a specific portion of text or content within a larger block of text. <span> elements are often used to apply CSS styles, such as color, font size, font weight, etc., to individual words or phrases within a paragraph. It does not affect the layout of the document and is typically used for small-scale styling or scripting purposes. Examples: <span class="highlight">, <span style="color: red;">.

subjective.question: How to convert HTML code to XHTML? Write 4 points.
subjective.answer: To convert HTML code to XHTML: • Add an XML declaration (<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>). • Replace the HTML doctype with an XHTML doctype. • Ensure all elements have proper closing tags. • Quote all attribute values using double quotes.

subjective.question: Why do we use comments?
subjective.answer: Comments in markup languages like HTML serve to enhance code readability and understanding. They act as documentation, clarify complex sections, aid debugging, facilitate communication within teams, and enable temporary code adjustments without deletion. Overall, they are essential for code maintenance and collaboration.

subjective.question: Define URL.
subjective.answer: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location and, optionally, a protocol for accessing it. It serves as a standardized way to identify resources on the internet. The following questions are NOT from any past paper. They were created from the topics that recur most often in the MCQ sources for this course (see the header disclosure), and each is given with a model answer.

subjective.question: Write the basic structure of an HTML5 document and briefly explain each part.
subjective.answer: <!DOCTYPE html> <html> <head> <title>Page Title</title> </head> <body> Page content goes here. </body> </html> • <!DOCTYPE html> — declaration that tells the browser this is an HTML5 document; it must be the very first line. • <html> — the root element that wraps the whole document. • <head> — contains information about the document (metadata) that is not displayed, such as the title and links to CSS. • <title> — defines the title of the document, shown in the browser tab. • <body> — contains all the visible content of the web page (headings, paragraphs, images, links, etc.).

subjective.question: Differentiate between the id selector and the class selector in CSS, with the syntax of each.
subjective.answer: id selector: • Selects one unique element whose id attribute matches; an id can be used only once on a page. • It is defined with a hash (#) character. • Example: #header { color: blue; } applies to <div id="header">. class selector: • Selects all elements with the given class attribute; the same class can be used on many elements. • It is defined with a period (.) character. • Example: .highlight { color: red; } applies to every element with class="highlight".

subjective.question: Explain the four CSS position values: static, relative, absolute and fixed.
subjective.answer: • static — the default position. The element follows the normal flow of the page and is not affected by top/bottom/left/right properties. • relative — the element is positioned relative to its normal (original) position; setting top/left moves it from where it would normally be, without affecting other elements. • absolute — the element is positioned relative to its nearest positioned ancestor (or the page if none) and is removed from the normal flow, so it can overlap other elements. • fixed — the element is positioned relative to the browser window and does not move even if the page is scrolled.

subjective.question: What is the difference between "visibility: hidden" and "display: none" in CSS?
subjective.answer: • visibility: hidden — the element is hidden (not visible), but it still takes up its space in the layout of the page. • display: none — the element is completely removed from display and takes up no space, as if it did not exist on the page.

subjective.question: Write any five rules for naming variables in JavaScript.
subjective.answer: 1. Variable names can contain letters, digits, underscores (_) and dollar signs ($). 2. A variable name must begin with a letter, underscore (_) or dollar sign ($) — it cannot begin with a number. 3. Variable names are case sensitive (age and Age are different variables). 4. A variable name cannot contain spaces; multiple words are joined, e.g. using camelCase like firstName. 5. Reserved words (keywords) of JavaScript, such as var, function or return, cannot be used as variable names.

subjective.question: Differentiate between the == and === operators in JavaScript, with examples.
subjective.answer: • == (equality operator) compares only the values of two operands; it converts the operands to a common type before comparison. Example: 1 == "1" returns true. • === (strict equality operator) compares both the value and the data type of the operands; no type conversion is done. Example: 1 === "1" returns false, because one is a number and the other is a string.

subjective.question: Write the value returned by each of the following JavaScript expressions: (a) Math.ceil(7.4) (b) Math.round(8.4) (c) Math.floor(7.9) (d) Math.max(5.2, -5.2, 6.2, -6.2)
subjective.answer: (a) Math.ceil(7.4) = 8 — ceil rounds a number up to the nearest integer. (b) Math.round(8.4) = 8 — round gives the nearest integer (0.5 and above round up). (c) Math.floor(7.9) = 7 — floor rounds a number down to the nearest integer. (d) Math.max(5.2, -5.2, 6.2, -6.2) = 6.2 — max returns the largest of the given numbers.

subjective.question: How can an array be created in JavaScript? Explain the pop() and sort() functions with examples.
subjective.answer: An array is created with square brackets, for example: var students = ["Ali", "Ahmed", "Sara"]; • pop() — removes the last element of an array (and returns it). Example: students.pop(); removes "Sara". • sort() — sorts the elements of an array (by default in alphabetical/ascending order). Example: students.sort(); arranges the names in alphabetical order.

subjective.topic: Web Technologies: HTTP, XML, AJAX & jQuery
subjective.question: Differentiate between the GET and POST methods used to send data to a server.
subjective.answer: GET: • Requests data from a specified resource. • Data is sent in the URL, so it is visible and its length is limited. • Requests can be cached by the client and bookmarked. POST: • Sends data to the server in the body of the request, not in the URL. • There is no practical limit on the amount of data, and the data is not visible in the address bar. • Requests are not cached and cannot be bookmarked.

subjective.topic: Web Technologies: HTTP, XML, AJAX & jQuery
subjective.question: Write any four naming rules for XML elements.
subjective.answer: 1. Element names can contain letters, numbers and other characters (such as underscore). 2. Element names cannot start with a number or punctuation character. 3. Element names cannot start with the letters xml (or XML, Xml, etc.). 4. Element names cannot contain spaces. (Also note: XML element names are case sensitive, so <Name> and <name> are different elements.)

subjective.topic: Web Technologies: HTTP, XML, AJAX & jQuery
subjective.question: What is AJAX? What is the role of the responseText property?
subjective.answer: AJAX (Asynchronous JavaScript and XML) is a technique for updating parts of a web page with data from the server without reloading the whole page. It uses the XMLHttpRequest object to send and receive data in the background (asynchronously). The responseText property holds the response data received from the server as a text string; the JavaScript code reads this string and uses it to update the page content.

subjective.topic: Web Technologies: HTTP, XML, AJAX & jQuery
subjective.question: What is jQuery? What is the purpose of the $(document).ready() function?
subjective.answer: jQuery is a fast, small and feature-rich JavaScript library that simplifies HTML document traversing and manipulation, event handling and animation. Its selectors start with the $ sign. The $(document).ready() function allows us to execute a function when the document (DOM) is fully loaded and ready to be worked with, so the script does not run before the page elements exist: $(document).ready(function() { // code to run when the page is loaded });

subjective.question: How many parts does a URL have? Define each part in detail.
subjective.answer: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is made up of the following parts: • Protocol (Scheme): e.g. http:// or https:// — it tells the browser how to access the resource. • Host / Domain Name: e.g. www.vu.edu.pk — the address of the server where the resource is stored (www is the subdomain). • Port: an optional number, e.g. :80 — the communication port on the server used for the connection. • Path: e.g. /lectures/cs202.html — the location of the file or folder on the server. • Query String: an optional part beginning with "?" — it passes data to the server as key=value pairs joined by "&". • Fragment (Anchor): an optional part beginning with "#" — it points to a specific section within the page.

subjective.question: Write six characteristics of a Dynamic URL.
subjective.answer: 1. It is generated dynamically by a web application, usually from a database, when a user requests the page. 2. It contains a query string beginning with "?" that carries parameters as name=value pairs joined by "&". 3. It contains special characters such as ?, &, =, % and +. 4. Its content changes according to the user, the session or the search criteria. 5. It is usually long and difficult to read, remember and type manually. 6. It is less friendly for search engines and for bookmarking than a static URL.

subjective.question: Write about CSS selectors.
subjective.answer: A CSS selector is the part of a CSS rule that selects (targets) the HTML element or elements to which the styles will be applied. The main types of selectors are: • Element (Type) Selector: selects all elements of a given tag, e.g. p { color: blue; } • id Selector: selects the single element having a specific id; it is written with a # sign, e.g. #header { } • Class Selector: selects all elements having a specific class; it is written with a dot, e.g. .green { } • Universal Selector: selects every element on the page; it is written as * { } • Group Selector: applies the same style to several selectors separated by commas, e.g. h1, h2, p { } • Descendant Selector: selects elements that are inside another element, written with a space, e.g. div p { }

subjective.question: Name the selector used for selecting all h1 elements, and name the selector which can select all of the elements on a page.
subjective.answer: All h1 elements are selected with the element (type) selector, written simply as the tag name: h1 { } All elements on the page are selected with the universal selector, written as an asterisk: * { } For example, * { color: green; } applies the style to every element. (Elements having class="green" in the HTML are selected with the class selector .green { }.)

subjective.question: Write three different ways to use the border-color property in CSS.
subjective.answer: The value of the border-color property can be given in three different ways (all three examples below set the same red color): 1. By color name: border-color: red; 2. By HEX value: border-color: #FF0000; 3. By RGB value: border-color: rgb(255, 0, 0);

subjective.question: A font size of 32 pixels is equal to how many em?
subjective.answer: The em is a relative unit of measurement equal to the current font size. Taking the standard default base font size of 16 pixels, 1em = 16px, therefore: 32px ÷ 16px = 2em So a font size of 32 pixels is equal to 2em.

subjective.question: Write short details of the window.open(), window.close(), window.moveTo() and window.resizeTo() methods — what does each function do?
subjective.answer: • window.open(): opens a new browser window or tab and loads the specified URL in it; the URL, window name and features such as width and height can be passed to it. • window.close(): closes the current browser window (normally, a window can only be closed by the script that opened it). • window.moveTo(x, y): moves the window to the specified absolute position, given by the x and y coordinates, on the screen. • window.resizeTo(width, height): resizes the window to the specified width and height, measured in pixels.

subjective.question: Enlist some drawbacks of JavaScript.
subjective.answer: • Security: JavaScript code runs on the user's computer and its source can be viewed by anyone, so it can be misused and cannot be trusted for sensitive work. • Browser dependence: JavaScript is interpreted by the browser, and different browsers may interpret the same code differently. • It can be disabled: if the user disables JavaScript in the browser, all its functionality stops working. • No file access: JavaScript cannot read or write files on the user's computer. • No multithreading: JavaScript is single-threaded and does not support multiprocessing. • Rendering problems: a JavaScript error can stop the whole web page from rendering properly.
